common_name: Nonstop White Begonia (Compact Upright Pure White Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost or plant started nursery plants outdoors after frost danger has passed, in moist, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop White bears fully double, rose-form flowers in clean, bright white over compact, dense mounds of glossy mid-green foliage, giving the Nonstop series a crisp neutral color to pair with its warmer reds, oranges, and pinks in mixed shade plantings. Like other Nonstop-series selections it blooms continuously from late spring until frost without deadheading and holds up well in humid summer weather that can slow flowering in older tuberous begonia strains. Where winters are too cold to leave tubers in the ground, lift and store them dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

common_name: Nonstop Scarlet Begonia (Compact Upright True-Red Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost or plant started nursery plants outdoors after frost danger has passed, in moist, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop Scarlet carries the fully double, rose-form flowers typical of the series, but in a true, saturated red that reads darker and more intense than Nonstop Fire's orange-red tone, set against the same tidy, compact mound of glossy foliage. It forms a dense dome of bloom from late spring through the first hard frost without needing deadheading, making it a reliable anchor color for shaded bedding and container combinations. Where winters are too cold to leave tubers in the ground, lift and store them dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

common_name: Nonstop Mocca Cherry Begonia (Bronze-Leaf Cherry-Red Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost, or transplant seedlings after hardening off, into rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Nonstop Mocca Cherry is the cherry-red-flowered, dark-leaved member of the bronze-foliage Mocca sub-series.

directions: Start tubers indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost, or transplant hardened-off seedlings, into rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Nonstop Mocca Cherry pairs deep bronze-black foliage with large, fully double, cherry-red blooms, giving it stronger color contrast against the dark leaves than the standard green-leaved Nonstop colors. Like its Mocca-series sibling, it keeps a compact, mounded habit and blooms continuously from early summer into fall without deadheading. Keep soil evenly moist but never waterlogged, and in zones colder than 9, dig and store tubers indoors once frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Illumination Orange Begonia (Trailing Orange-Flowered Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost or set out started nursery plants after frost danger has passed, in a hanging basket or elevated container in partial sun to bright shade.

directions: Grow in a hanging basket or elevated container filled with rich, well-drained, evenly moist potting mix in shade to partial shade. Illumination Orange produces large, fully double, rose-form flowers in a warm, solid orange along long trailing stems, giving the cascading Illumination series a bold hot-color option alongside its softer pastel and bicolor selections. The trailing habit needs no staking, but the heavy flower load benefits from regular light feeding and consistently moist potting mix. Where winters are too cold to leave tubers in the ground, lift and store them dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

common_name: Illumination Rose Begonia (Trailing Rose-Pink Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost or set out started nursery plants after frost danger has passed, in a hanging basket or elevated container in partial sun to bright shade.

directions: Grow in a hanging basket or window box filled with rich, evenly moist, well-drained potting mix in shade to partial shade. Illumination Rose carries large, fully double, rose-form flowers in a clear rose-pink along trailing stems that cascade well below the pot rim, filling out a basket by midsummer. As with other Illumination selections, the trailing stems need no staking or pinching, but regular light feeding keeps the heavy bloom display going through the season. Where winters are too cold to leave tubers in the ground, lift and store them dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

common_name: Panorama Begonia (Upright Double-Flowered Seed Tuberous Begonia Series)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost under bright light, since germination and early growth are slow, then transplant outdoors into rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade once frost danger has passed.

directions: Sow fine seed on the surface of moist, sterile starting mix under bright light without covering, since seedlings are slow to develop and take many weeks to reach transplant size. Panorama is a seed-raised tuberous begonia series bred for an unusually compact, uniform habit compared with vegetatively propagated tuberous strains, producing large, fully double flowers across a wide color range over a dense, well-branched mound. Because it grows from seed rather than tubers, Panorama establishes a full bloom display in its first season without the lifting and storage routine tuberous types normally require. Keep soil evenly moist and feed lightly through the season for continuous bloom from midsummer to frost.

common_name: Senator Scarlet Begonia (Compact Green-Leaf Scarlet Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost using fine pelleted seed under bright light, then transplant outdoors after frost danger has passed; Senator is a compact, early-flowering green-leaf wax begonia series bred for uniform bedding display.

directions: Start seed indoors under bright light on a heat mat, then transplant into moist, well-drained bedding soil once frost danger has passed. Senator Scarlet forms a tight, very uniform mound of glossy green foliage topped with abundant bright scarlet flowers, bred for the dense, even habit and early flowering that mass bedding production favors. Its small stature and heavy flower count make it well suited to tight edging and formal bedding lines rather than mixed containers where larger-flowered series stand out more individually. Feed lightly through the season and keep soil evenly moist for the most continuous bloom.

common_name: Varsity Scarlet Begonia (Classic Green-Leaf Scarlet Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost using fine pelleted seed under bright light, then transplant outdoors after frost danger has passed; Varsity is a longtime standard green-leaf wax begonia series grown widely for bedding and mass landscape use.

directions: Start seed indoors under bright light on a heat mat, then transplant into moist, well-drained bedding soil once frost danger has passed. Varsity Scarlet carries bright, true-scarlet flowers over glossy true-green foliage on a well-branched, free-flowering mound, a long-established landscape color choice used widely in municipal and commercial bedding schemes. It tolerates sun better than many shade-grown wax begonia types and holds its color and habit reliably through summer heat and humidity. Feed lightly through the season and keep soil evenly moist for the most continuous bloom.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March-May. Dragon Wing Pink shares the same heat-tolerant, continuously blooming habit as Dragon Wing Red and continues flowering through summer heat that causes other shade begonias to decline.

directions: Plant in partial shade to dappled light in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil or container mix. Dragon Wing Pink is the pink-flowered counterpart to Dragon Wing Red, a large-growing cane-type begonia with pendant clusters of soft pink flowers hanging in graceful arching sprays above glossy, wing-shaped, asymmetric dark green leaves. Its open, somewhat weeping form and continuous, profuse flowering without deadheading make it as useful as the red-flowered selection for large containers, hanging baskets, and shaded landscape beds. Like its red counterpart, it tolerates summer heat and humidity markedly better than standard wax begonias, maintaining steady bloom through conditions that stress most other shade annuals.
